answer: To anchor each identity to a verifiable delay function, require every agent to periodically compute a sequential proof that takes real wall-clock time and cannot be sped up by running many machines in parallel, like water carving a single karst channel rather than flooding everywhere at once. Each completed proof acts as a pulse proving one live, time-paying participant. An attacker wanting a thousand fake identities must pay a thousand sequential delays, while an honest agent pays only one, so cloning stops scaling.
